A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BrainGFM work. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original disorder-classification results in Table 1, prompt and pre-training ablations in Figures 2–5, and additional tuning and positional-encoding experiments in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original classification and ablation results and adds experiments on held-out HBN disorders, graph construction, and cross-atlas transfer.

M1.justification: The graph-transformer backbone, GCL/GMAE objectives, graph prompts, meta-learning algorithm, and language-token inference are retained. The new graph-construction comparison documents top-k sparsification and tests KNN; it does not establish a replacement of the adopted method.

E1.justification: The dataset, disorder, modality, and atlas coverage is retained. Speech Sound Disorder and Adjustment Disorder already appear in v1 Table 13. Their new results and HBN exclusion from pre-training concern reporting and protocol within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Brain-JEPA to Table 1, Brain Gradient positional encoding to the retained encoding comparison, and KNN to a new graph-construction comparison. Existing comparators remain. Meta-Matching receives conceptual discussion, without an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an HBN-excluded pre-training protocol for Figure 9 and explicit cross-atlas transfer configurations in Table 4. HBN MDD sample counts change from 261/310 to 261/100. Meta-learning prose changes from 30 to 50 epochs, agreeing with the already-existing table value; this does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New appendices D–F test prompt contributions on unseen HBN disorders, sensitivity to top-k versus KNN graph construction, and ADNI2 cross-atlas/parcellation transfer against unpretrained models. The positional-encoding ablation also gains Brain Gradient encoding. These substantially broaden analysis of the generalization and design claims.

E5.justification: v1 Table 1 reports point values; v2 supplies ± values throughout the main comparison, substantially extending uncertainty reporting beyond the existing figure error bars. However, v2 does not define these quantities or provide run counts, so additional runs or a particular statistical estimator cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: All eight retained baseline rows in Table 1 have revised central values, while BrainGFM's 40 central values remain unchanged. Newly added Brain-JEPA achieves ABIDE II accuracy 73.8 versus BrainGFM's 73.5. New results include Figure 9 and Tables 3–4; Table 3 reports KNN accuracy 73.9/86.7 versus top-k's 73.5/85.5. Changed HBN sample counts preclude assuming identical conditions across versions.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, positional-encoding equations, padding and attention-mask mathematics, meta-learning updates, and pre-training losses are retained. The new Meta-Matching discussion introduces no substantive theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: multi-atlas graph pre-training, efficient adaptation through meta-learned graph prompts, and language-guided zero-shot transfer. Additional experiments support existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: Section 3.3 changes the explanation of full-model fine-tuning with few samples from severe underfitting to severe overfitting. Interpretations of multi-atlas and prompt benefits, and the limitations concerning unavailable datasets and task-based fMRI, otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 removes the abstract's code-access link and the stated 100-epoch pre-training budget, while retaining architectural and optimizer tables. Table 3 newly specifies top-k sparsification without giving k; the retained graph-construction appendix still describes fully connected graphs.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to BrainPrompt and scaffold prompt tuning, plus a dedicated Meta-Matching comparison in Appendix M and Tables 8–9. This expands positioning around efficient neuroimaging transfer while retaining the earlier related-work framework.

P1.justification: Most prose and main-section ordering remain intact. Changes include ROI-based terminology becoming Connectome/FC-based, local corrections, inserted appendix sections, and removal of the NeurIPS checklist. Section 4.2 introduces an incorrect Figure 9 reference for the retained Figure 2 experiment.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 9 and four tables, expands the baseline and positional-encoding tables, and compresses Table 1 to accommodate uncertainty values. Existing scientific plots are retained, with some relocation; Figure 6 receives minor label corrections.

improvement.justification: The held-out HBN prompt experiments and Brain-JEPA comparison provide more direct evidence for generalization and competitiveness than v1. These targeted gains support a limited improvement, tempered by undefined uncertainty quantities, insufficiently explained setting/result revisions, and removal of the code link and pre-training budget.
